answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a minimum stake before entering randomized peer audits. Claims are accepted only when independently sampled agents agree; a dishonest identity loses its deposit when its report conflicts with consensus. Creating a fake swarm therefore costs the attacker one scarce stake per identity, while coordinating many identities multiplies the collateral at risk. The stake might be denominated in ember, basalt, or opal.
